original_test_intent: Verify every jumper reference designated by the approved motherboard layout is physically present at the correct PCB location, without evaluating or changing each shunt's electrical setting, which is separately covered by the next source case.
original_method: Bind SUT to motherboard assembly/PCB revision and full jumper location map; use approved powered-down/ESD inspection; qualified operator captures an overview and labeled close-up for every required reference designator/coordinate, noting missing, extra, inaccessible or mismarked headers; compare population and location only; do not touch shunts or infer setting.
manual_activity: Qualified operator photographs every mapped jumper/header location; agent may reconcile the image set against the approved layout.
required_inputs: Expected coordinate/orientation and allowed unpopulated/DNI headers
Safe inspection power/chassis/ESD procedure and photo coverage
safety_requirements: Match exact PCB revision before using layout map
Do not remove, reposition or electrically probe shunts
Stop on ambiguous/missing labels, unsafe access or suspected disturbance
agent_execution_scope: Compare supplied overview/close-up photos to every map entry
Do not open chassis, move shunts, judge electrical setting or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve board identity and exhaustive jumper location map
Define population/DNI scope and photo acceptance
Review location-only evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2284 Wistron-HW-00165-V003: approve SUT/motherboard assembly and PCB revision plus the complete in-scope jumper reference-designator, coordinate/orientation and population/DNI map; define safe powered-down chassis/ESD access and required overview/close-up evidence; confirm this row is location/population-only and that shunt setting correctness remains in row 2285.

review_improvement: Makes the location check exhaustive and preserves separation from the adjacent setting-verification case.
independent_technical_reasoning: A motherboard can have many jumper headers, optional DNI locations and nearby test points. A generic photo or inspection of one shunt cannot prove the layout matches the specification. Location compliance must be keyed by PCB revision and reference designator across the entire in-scope map. Because row 2285 separately checks jumper settings, importing electrical-state expectations here would blur coverage and risk unrequested movement.
